headline: Computational correction and calibration of RNA sequencing quantities
label: Rna Sequencing Computational Calibration Tools
summary: Preprints now pair RT-PCR residuals, gene-specific normalization and AnnData-native tooling with long-read benchmarking to tighten RNA-seq quantification.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational correction and calibration of RNA sequencing quantities. BRAID calibrates RNA-seq splicing ΔPSI estimates with split conformal intervals derived from RT-PCR residuals, reporting 0.971 RT-PCR coverage across 139 cassette exons. gecco proposes gene-specific exponent-corrected normalization for bulk RNA-seq counts to remove residual library size bias while preserving signal. pylimma offers a Python port of R limma for differential expression, native to AnnData and validated against R across 227 function comparisons and six datasets. MKMC provides reference-free k-mer analysis for RNA-seq that matches alignment-based differential expression. A systematic benchmark of ten tools for single-cell and spatial Nanopore long-read RNA-seq adds an evaluation perspective. Other items, including the Blood RNA Stability Atlas, AtlasLens, FRACTEL, and PerturbMatch, address adjacent analysis problems in atlas exploration and perturbation screens rather than sharing this focus.
